details:
Project Details – Martian Cats

Martian Cats is an interactive, browser-based space exploration game that lets players design, build, and operate their own spacecraft before taking it on a mission. Players choose a destination, such as the Moon, Mars, Europa, or an asteroid, and assemble a spacecraft by balancing factors like mass, power, budget, communication range, heat management, and propellant. Every design decision affects the mission, introducing players to the real trade-offs involved in space exploration.

The game takes players through the complete mission journey, from spacecraft preparation and launch to spaceflight, landing, and surface operations. Different difficulty levels introduce varying mission constraints, while multiplayer support allows up to four players to collaborate on the same device.

The project incorporates NASA resources, including imagery, Perseverance rover photographs, Near-Earth Object data, space-weather notifications, and NASA 3D models, adding scientific context to the gameplay.

Martian Cats aims to make complex aerospace concepts more accessible through interactive learning rather than passive reading. Its creative approach combines spacecraft design, physics-based calculations, resource management, and game mechanics into one connected mission experience. During development, the team considered scientific relevance, gameplay clarity, accessibility, mission realism, and the consequences of player decisions.
